To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

aging is associated with the formation of ectopic branches of neurons in the nematode Caenorhabditish elegans, and that the incidence of branching is influenced by two signaling pathways that can alter the rate of aging.

the nervous system in aging animals displays spontaneous neurite branching, which correlates with a loss of function and that the rate at which this branching occurs can be influenced by two pathways, the Jun kinase (JNK) and insulin/IGF-like (daf-2) signaling pathways, that can affect the overall rate of animal aging.
neurons in the nervous system of aging animals frequently display ectopic branches and the incidence of branching is influenced by pathways that affect the rate at which animals age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of morphological and physiological changes that occur in C. elegans with age.
the analysis of the mechanisms that regulate the growth of neurites in C. elegans.
the study of the mechanisms that regulate neurite branching in the nervous system of the nematode C. elegans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the aging of the nervous system in C. elegans is characterized by the growth of new branches from existing neurons.
the aging process in C. elegans is associated with a spontaneous growth of neurites in the nervous system.

age-related neurite branching in the nervous system of C. elegans is a novel form of growth in normal animals that is accelerated by JNK signaling, suppressed by insulin/IGF-like signaling, and that is correlated with a decline in sensory function and mobility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aging can be a growth process.
aging can promote growth of neurites in the nervous system, and this growth can occur in the absence of tissue damage.
aging is not only associated with loss of function, but also with aberrant function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nervous system is not immune to the effects of aging and that the aging process can have a profound influence on its structure.
aging can be a potent driver of neuronal growth, and this may be relevant to the pathogenesis of age-related neurological disease.
the nervous system is not exempt from the changes that occur with normal aging.
